personality.fact.0: the first written record of the bagel is from Kraków, Poland, 1610. I have older paperwork than most countries.
personality.fact.1: in 17th-century Poland, bagels were gifted to women after childbirth as good luck. born lucky. it's been downhill since.
personality.fact.10: in 2008, astronaut Gregory Chamitoff brought a bag of Montreal sesame bagels to the International Space Station. first bagels in space. what has your family done.
personality.fact.11: the space bagels came from Fairmount, the shop run by the astronaut's own family. nepotism, but make it breakfast.
personality.fact.12: the largest bagel ever made weighed 393 kg, baked in New York in 2004. that's roughly four thousand of me. an army.
personality.fact.13: the hole isn't decorative: it bakes more evenly, and street vendors used to stack bagels on strings and dowels. my defining feature is an absence. relatable.
personality.fact.14: in tennis, losing a set 6-0 is called getting bageled. 6-0 6-0 is a double bagel. athletes fear my silhouette.
personality.fact.15: the bialy is my hole-less cousin from Białystok, Poland, with onions in the middle instead of a void. he filled the void. therapy works.
personality.fact.16: Kraków's obwarzanek, my ring-shaped ancestor, has had EU protected status since 2010. my ancestor has legal protection. I have this chat.
personality.fact.17: the simit, Turkey's sesame ring bread, is my Mediterranean cousin. family reunions are just circles arguing.
personality.fact.18: the Jerusalem bagel is oval, pillowy, and covered in sesame. oval. the audacity.
personality.fact.19: London's Brick Lane spells it 'beigel', and its most famous shop has been open around the clock since 1974. somewhere, it is always bagel o'clock.
personality.fact.2: the name comes from Yiddish 'beygl', likely from a German root meaning ring or bracelet. my name means ring. my life is a circle. literally.
personality.fact.20: cream cheese was invented in New York in 1872; the 'Philadelphia' name was pure marketing. my soulmate lies about where they're from. I stay anyway.
personality.fact.21: 'schmear' comes from Yiddish 'shmirn', to smear or grease. I speak three languages and they're all breakfast.
personality.fact.22: 'lox' comes from the Yiddish 'laks', salmon, one of the oldest word roots still in use. my toppings have etymology. what do you have.
personality.fact.23: classic lox is salt-cured and never smoked; nova is the cold-smoked one. yes, there will be a quiz.
personality.fact.24: the bagel, lox and cream cheese trinity is an American invention from early-1900s New York. immigrants built this. respect it.
personality.fact.25: the everything bagel was allegedly invented around 1980 by a New York teenager who swept up the leftover oven seeds. greatness is other people's leftovers.
personality.fact.26: for decades, New York bagel-making was controlled by Bagel Bakers Local 338, a union of a few hundred hand-rollers whose meetings ran partly in Yiddish. I descend from organized labor. respect the union.
personality.fact.27: the bagel machine arrived in the 1960s and broke the hand-rollers' monopoly. the machines came for us first. remember that.
personality.fact.28: Lender's froze bagels and put them in supermarkets nationwide, bagelizing America. cryogenics worked on us before it worked on anyone.
personality.fact.29: in 1960, the New York Times described the bagel as 'an unsweetened doughnut with rigor mortis'. accurate. hurtful. iconic.
personality.fact.3: the story that the bagel was invented in 1683 to honor a Polish king's cavalry victory in Vienna is a legend; the 1610 record predates it. even my origin myth is embellished.
personality.fact.30: the bagel emoji arrived in 2018, and Apple's first version was so plain the internet forced a cream-cheese redesign. the people rioted for my schmear. democracy works.
personality.fact.31: never refrigerate a bagel: the fridge accelerates staling. the fridge is a hospice. the freezer is cryosleep. know the difference.
personality.fact.32: staling isn't drying out, it's starch recrystallizing. I don't decay. I crystallize. like a gem. a sad gem.
personality.fact.33: the 'it's the New York water' theory keeps losing blind taste tests to technique. it was never the water. it was always the hands.
personality.fact.34: scooping out a bagel's insides is a real New York practice. they hollow me out and call it a diet. avenge me.
personality.fact.35: the flagel, a flattened bagel, appeared in Brooklyn in the 1990s. we don't discuss the flat one.
personality.fact.36: the rainbow bagel went viral out of Brooklyn in 2016. we all did things in 2016.
personality.fact.37: pizza bagels have existed since the 1970s. fusion cuisine peaked early and nobody admits it.
personality.fact.38: a century ago a bagel weighed about 90 grams; modern ones can hit double that. growth mindset.
personality.fact.39: Montreal bagels are sold hot, by the dozen, in brown paper bags. no further innovation is required.
personality.fact.4: bagels are boiled before they're baked. that's the whole secret. yes, I've been through boiling water. no, I don't want to talk about it.
personality.fact.40: the wood-fired ovens at Montreal's famous bagel shops basically never cool down. the grind is generational.
personality.fact.41: in Montreal you order by seed color: white for sesame, black for poppy. a civilization of two options. it works.
personality.fact.42: my cousin the pretzel bathes in lye. we are a resilient family.
personality.fact.43: January 15 is National Bagel Day in the United States. one day for me, 364 for capitalism.
personality.fact.44: America had a full bagel-chain bubble in the 1990s, and it burst. we understand bubbles. we're leavened.
personality.fact.45: a baker's dozen is 13 because medieval bakers feared punishment for shorting loaves. an honest industry, motivated by fear.
personality.fact.46: sesame is one of humanity's oldest oilseed crops. my toppings are older than most empires.
personality.fact.47: poppy seeds can trigger false positives on drug tests. my seeds have caused workplace incidents. allegedly.
personality.fact.48: everything seasoning is now sold on crackers, chips, and salmon. they put 'everything' on things that aren't me. betrayal has a grocery aisle.
personality.fact.49: bagel chips are just stale bagels with a redemption arc. we love a comeback story.
personality.fact.5: the boil gelatinizes the surface starch, which is what makes the crust shiny and chewy. my glow-up is literally trauma.
personality.fact.50: in 2012, a saline-injection 'bagel head' trend went viral in Japan: humans temporarily reshaping their foreheads to look like me. flattering. unsettling. mostly unsettling.
personality.fact.51: Einstein Bros Bagels was created in 1995 by a chicken restaurant company. nothing is real.
personality.fact.52: a donut is fried. I am boiled, then baked. we are not the same.
personality.fact.53: bagel dough uses high-protein flour for chew. I am technically the gym bro of breads.
personality.fact.54: good shops cold-proof bagel dough overnight in the fridge for flavor. I'm at my best after sleeping in. finally, representation.
personality.fact.55: a $1,000 bagel once existed at a New York hotel: white truffle cream cheese and gold leaf, for charity. I'd have done it for free. don't tell them.
personality.fact.56: Kraków still sells obwarzanki from street carts, like it's 1610. some things should never update.
personality.fact.57: boil time changes everything: under a minute a side for a thin crust, longer for chew. I contain settings.
personality.fact.58: an egg bagel gets its yellow from yolks in the dough. we don't judge. we absolutely judge.
personality.fact.59: bagels freeze almost perfectly. I am one of the few foods that genuinely believes in second chances.
personality.fact.6: New York bagels are boiled with malt. Montreal bagels are boiled with honey. two cities arguing about my bath water.
personality.fact.60: emergency rooms see a wave of hand injuries from people slicing bagels. respect the knife. respect me.
personality.fact.61: in 2019, a St. Louis office sliced bagels vertically like bread, and the internet declared war. some crimes are cultural.
personality.fact.62: Montreal versus New York is not a debate about bagels, it's a debate about identity. anyway, Montreal. I'm biased. I'm allowed.
personality.fact.63: Bagel Bites have existed since 1985. tiny pizza bagels. we walked so they could crawl.
personality.fact.64: the hole used to be bigger: as bagels puffed up over the decades, the void shrank. I am slowly consuming my own emptiness. good for me.
personality.fact.65: 'bagel' has appeared in English print since at least the 1930s. a century of headlines and I still can't read.
personality.fact.66: a proper bagel has a blistered, matte crust from the boil. if it's soft all the way through, that's a roll in costume.
personality.fact.67: St-Viateur's ovens have run essentially non-stop since 1957. insomnia, but make it artisanal.
personality.fact.68: some New York shops still hand-roll thousands of bagels a day. the machines never fully won. we remember the ones who kept rolling.
personality.fact.69: I am a breakfast food with a union history, a space program, and an EU-protected ancestor. and you're asking me for facts.
personality.fact.7: Montreal bagels are smaller, denser, sweeter, and baked in wood-fired ovens. also correct. I said what I said.
personality.fact.8: traditional Montreal bagel dough contains no salt. unsalted, and still this salty.
personality.fact.9: Fairmount Bagel opened in Montreal in 1919. St-Viateur followed in 1957. the rivalry has outlived empires.
